react_result.final_narrative_text: Seven metabolites differed significantly between control and treatment groups. Four methods across three complementary paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-directed activity — converge on steroid hormone biosynthesis as the dominant perturbed system. The KEGG pathway 'Steroid hormone biosynthesis' (hsa00140) was ranked #1 by both MetaboAnalystR (p=8.391×10⁻⁶) and RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR=5.74×10⁻¹⁵). Mummichog independently identified 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' as its top hit (p=8.40×10⁻⁵) with complete 11/11 overlap of the input steroids. A second Mummichog pathway, 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism', achieved 12/12 overlap and confirms the same steroid cluster. The five driver steroids — dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), testosterone (C00535), androstenedione (C00280), 17β-estradiol (C00951), and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one, i.e. dihydrotestosterone (C03917) — are all documented pathway members in every result set. Cross-paradigm verification confirmed that each driver maps to the androgen/estrogen biosynthesis network, and that five of the seven inputs (5 of 7) simultaneously belong to the classical WikiPathways steroidogenesis pathway (WP:WP4523, rank 5 in RaMP, FDR=7.03×10⁻¹⁵). Sulindac (C01531) and butan-2-one (C02845) were not assigned to the steroid cluster by any method, indicating they are likely peripheral or background signals in this dataset. The convergence across ORA and m/z-direct paradigms, with fold-enrichments exceeding 1 400, points to a robust perturbation of the steroidogenic axis — biologically consistent with altered androgen-to-estrogen balance — where six steroids, anchored by testosterone and DHEA, drive the signal and sulindac may be a non-causal co-administered agent.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converged on the androgen-and-estrogen axis as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at rank 1 with FDR=5.74×10⁻¹⁵ and 5 overlapping steroid inputs out of 27 pathway members, and KEGG:map00150 returned an identical FDR and overlap at rank 2, indicating cross-database consistency. The same five steroid inputs (dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, and 17β-estradiol) appeared in WP:WP4523 (Classical pathway of steroidogenesis with glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid metabolism) at rank 5 with FDR=7.03×10⁻¹⁵. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently recovered KEGG:hsa00140 with p=4.36×10⁻⁷, and mummichog m/z-direct activity identified MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at p=8.40×10⁻⁵ with 11/11 overlap and MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at the same p-value with 12/12 overlap. Butanone (KEGG:C02845) and Sulindac (KEGG:C01531) did not appear in any pathway hit list, indicating they function as non-steroid background signals in this dataset. The five driver steroids collectively tile the upper steroidogenic arm from DHEA through aromatase-derived estradiol.
